key_insight: PyroDash teaches a small language model to decide token-by-token when to hand off to a frozen large model, trading off reasoning accuracy and inference cost without needing a separate router or LLM logit access.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical serving strategy for math-reasoning systems that need scalable deployment, enabling configurable accuracy-cost tradeoffs and much lower LLM usage in production.
method: SLM emits a control token during generation to trigger a single handoff to the LLM with the partial reasoning trace.
Training proceeds in three stages: control-token embedding learning, offloading-oriented supervised fine-tuning, and cost-aware alignment via Group Relative Policy Optimization.
The reward balances answer correctness against normalized inference cost, encouraging selective LLM use only when needed.
evidence_signal: Across five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, the method reaches different operating points; at λ=0.05 it averages 64.04% accuracy with 20.4% lower cost, and at λ=0.6 it cuts LLM usage to 1.90% token ratio and 0.012 calls per example while reducing cost from USD 49.36 to USD 1.78.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of the learned offloading policy, so miscalibrated control-token decisions could underuse the LLM on hard steps or overuse it and erode cost savings.
paper_title: PyroDash: Cost-Efficient Token-Level Small-Large Language Model Collaborative Inference
